_doc: Strum patterns for one 4/4 bar as 4 space-separated BEAT CELLS (beats 1 2 3 4). Each cell's LENGTH is its subdivision: 1=quarter, 2=eighths, 3=triplet, 4=sixteenths. Char per slot: D=downstroke, U=upstroke, x=muted chuck, .=no strike (slot 0 of a cell is the downbeat). Encoded in Hookpad as re-struck chords with empty notes. See music_chord_riff_fingerprint (Layer 2 = strike rhythm).
_doc2: A PUSH is the &4 of one bar sustaining across the next downbeat. It shows up as a pair: bar A ends with a struck &4 held long, and bar B has no strike on beat 1. simple-kind-of-life is that pair -- No Doubt hold Dm for two bars, then C for two, and the strum is identical on both chords. The push, not a chord change, is what makes the second bar feel different from the first.
